item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is materially closer to the frozen contract: Upload validates inputs, uses multipartbody.NewFile, and delegates to the existing FilesService.Add path without changing Add. B violates central compatibility and routing requirements by changing Add to eagerly consume every caller body and having Upload bypass Add through a new private method.","reasons":["A preserves FilesService.Add and routes Upload through it exactly as required.","A explicitly validates both an empty filename and nil content before multipart construction.","Both use the established multipartbody.NewFile helper, but B calls a new private add method instead of the contractually required existing Add method.","B changes Add's observable behavior and error semantics: it eagerly buffers the supplied reader and introduces a new wrapped \"read file body\" error. This conflicts with preserving Add as the lower-level caller-encoded API with unchanged behavior and may alter when reader failures occur and how errors are reported to existing callers."],"risks_a":["It adds an unrelated public PersonsService.UploadPicture API and tests, violating scope discipline and the instruction to add exactly the Files convenience API.","Upload tests do not assert uploaded content, and there are no visible tests for empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures.","The retry test verifies two requests but does not inspect the multipart body on both attempts."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, directly contradicting the required routing and centralization contract.","FilesService.Add is behaviorally changed to buffer all caller-encoded bodies, expanding scope and potentially increasing memory use for existing callers.","The original Add test is replaced, and there are no visible validation or source-reader-error tests for Upload; Upload also lacks explicit validation at its entry point and relies on helper behavior."]}
